newsitem.title: UK: Cable firms vow to continue BSkyB rate card battle.
newsitem.headline: Cable firms vow to continue BSkyB rate card battle.

text.p: UK cable operators on Monday criticised a decision by the Office of Fair Trading (OFT) to approve BSkyB's revised rate card for the supply of its channels to cable companies and vowed to continue to fight it.

The cable companies could now seek to take the issue to the European Commission. The "rate card" sets out the structure and price that satellite broadcaster BSkyB charges cable companies for their channels.
"We fail to see how today's announcement is in the consumers' interest," industry body the Cable Communications Association said in a statement.
"The new rate card will require the majority, if not all, cable television subscribers to pay for BSkyB services regardless of whether they want them or not."
"The cable industry will be considering the details of today's announcement, and the OFT's full report when it is published. The issue is not closed," it added.
The Association said it disagreed with the OFT's assertion that there had been few suggestions on how to amend the rate card and that there was no evidence of its adverse effects.
It said the industry had been seeking an opportunity to discuss the issues with the OFT.
The UK cable industry is going through a period of consolidation as Mercury, the UK arm of Cable & Wirless Plc, merges with the UK cable operations of NYNEX, Bell Canada International and Videotron.
